subject: chem
title: Organic Compounds Containing Oxygen
syllabus: Alcohols — identification of primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols, mechanism of dehydration. Phenols — acidic nature, electrophilic substitution reactions: halogenation, nitration and sulphonation, Reimer–Tiemann reaction. Ethers — structure. Aldehydes and ketones — nature of carbonyl group; nucleophilic addition to >C=O group, relative reactivities of aldehydes and ketones; important reactions such as nucleophilic addition reactions (addition of HCN, NH3 and its derivatives), Grignard reagent; oxidation; reduction (Wolff-Kishner and Clemmensen); acidity of α-hydrogen, aldol condensation, Cannizzaro reaction, haloform reaction; chemical tests to distinguish between aldehydes and ketones. Carboxylic acids — acidic strength and factors affecting it.

body: Classes by the carbinol carbon: 1°, 2°, 3°. Lucas (HCl/ZnCl_{2}): 3° turbid at once, 2° in ~5 min, 1° only on heating. Ceric ammonium nitrate: red.
Oxidation: 1° → aldehyde (PCC) → acid (K_{2}Cr_{2}O_{7}, KMnO_{4}); 2° → ketone; 3° resist. Cu at 573 K: 1° → aldehyde, 2° → ketone, 3° → alkene.
Dehydration (conc. H_{2}SO_{4}): 3° > 2° > 1°; 443 K → alkene, 413 K (excess alcohol) → ether. Iodoform: CH_{3}CH(OH)– (ethanol is the only 1° one).
Phenol (pKa 10) is more acidic than alcohols (~16): the phenoxide is resonance-stabilised. −R/−I groups (o/p-NO_{2}) raise acidity; p-nitrophenol 7.15, picric acid 0.4.

Ring is very activated: Br_{2} water → 2,4,6-tribromophenol; dilute HNO_{3} → o-/p-nitrophenol (o is steam volatile). Kolbe (CO_{2}/NaOH) → salicylic acid; Reimer–Tiemann (CHCl_{3}/NaOH) → salicylaldehyde.
Zn dust → benzene; FeCl_{3} → violet; phthalein test. Ethers: Williamson (RONa + 1° RX). HI cleaves R–O: alkyl aryl ethers give phenol + RI; 3° alkyl leaves as R–I (S_{N}1).

check.why: The Ar–O bond is not cleaved.

body: Rosenmund (RCOCl + H_{2}/Pd–BaSO_{4}), Stephen (RCN + SnCl_{2}/HCl), Etard (toluene + CrO_{2}Cl_{2}), Gattermann–Koch (benzene + CO/HCl), ozonolysis, alkyne hydration (Hg^{2+}).
Ketones: RCN + R′MgX → ketone; Friedel–Crafts acylation; 2° alcohol oxidation.

check.q: Toluene + CrO₂Cl₂, then H₃O⁺ is the

body: Nucleophilic addition: HCHO > RCHO > ArCHO > RCOR > ArCOR (steric + electronic). HCN, NaHSO_{3}, ROH (acetals), NH_{2}–Z (oxime, hydrazone, 2,4-DNP, semicarbazone).
With α-H: aldol (dil. NaOH) → β-hydroxy carbonyl → α,β-unsaturated; Claisen–Schmidt (ArCHO + ketone). No α-H aldehydes: Cannizzaro (conc. NaOH) → acid salt + alcohol.

Tests: Tollens — all aldehydes (and HCOOH); Fehling/Benedict — aliphatic aldehydes and α-hydroxy ketones, not ArCHO. Iodoform — CH_{3}CO–. Reductions: Clemmensen (Zn-Hg/HCl), Wolff–Kishner (N_{2}H_{4}/KOH) → CH_{2}.
Acidity: −I groups raise it (Cl_{3}CCOOH > Cl_{2}CHCOOH > ClCH_{2}COOH > CH_{3}COOH); the effect fades with distance; alkyl groups lower it. HCOOH > CH_{3}COOH; benzoic acid 4.2.

Preparation: oxidation of 1° alcohols/aldehydes/alkylbenzenes, nitrile hydrolysis, RMgX + CO_{2}. Reactions: NaHCO_{3} → CO_{2}; esterification; HVZ (X_{2}/red P → α-halo acid); soda-lime decarboxylation; LiAlH_{4} → RCH_{2}OH.

traps: Fehling does not react with aromatic aldehydes.
Methanol does NOT give iodoform; ethanol does.
HCOOH reduces Tollens (it has an H–C=O).
Anisole + HI gives phenol, never iodobenzene.
Bromination of phenol needs no Lewis acid.

steps.note: Name reactions for aldehydes and ketones
Acidity and reactions of carboxylic acids

pyq.q: Match List - I (Reactants) with List - II (Products): (A) Phenol, Zn/Δ (B) Phenol, CHCl_{3}, NaOH, HCl (C) Phenol, CO_{2}, NaOH, HCl (D) Phenol, Conc. HNO_{3}; (I) Salicylaldehyde (II) Salicylic acid (III) Benzene (IV) Picric acid
sol: Zn dust removes O → benzene. Reimer–Tiemann → salicylaldehyde. Kolbe (CO_{2}, NaOH) → salicylic acid.
Conc. HNO_{3} → 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid).

pyq.q: Given below are two statement : Statement I : Bromination of phenol in solvent with low polarity such as CHCl_{3} or CS_{2} requires Lewis acid catalyst. Statement II : The lewis acid catalyst polarises the bromine to generate Br^{+}. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: The –OH activates the ring so strongly that Br_{2} in CS_{2} gives o/p-bromophenol with NO catalyst. I false.
II is the general role of FeBr_{3}/AlCl_{3}. True.
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Picric acid is 2, 4, 6-trinitrotoluene. Statement II : Phenol-2, 4-disulphuric acid is treated with conc. HNO_{3} to get picric acid. In the light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sol: Picric acid is 2,4,6-trinitroPHENOL (TNT is the toluene). I incorrect.
Sulphonating first, then nitrating (the –SO_{3}H groups are replaced) is the standard route. II correct.
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

pyq.q: In Reimer - Tiemann reaction, phenol is converted into salicylaldehyde through an intermediate. The structure of intermediate is _______.
sol: :CCl_{2} (from CHCl_{3} + OH^{−}) attacks the phenoxide ortho position → sodium o-(dichloromethyl)phenoxide.
Its hydrolysis (then acid) gives salicylaldehyde.

pyq.q: What amount of bromine will be required to convert 2 g of phenol into 2,4,6-tribromophenol? (Given molar mass in g mol^{−1} of C, H, O, Br are 12, 1, 16, 80 respectively)

Given below are two statements: Statement (I): The boiling points of alcohols and phenols increase with increase in the number of C - atoms. Statement (II): The boiling points of alcohols and phenols are higher in comparison to other class of compounds such as ethers, haloalkanes. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: I: larger molecules → stronger van der Waals forces. True.
II: intermolecular H-bonding raises b.p. above ethers/haloalkanes of similar mass. True.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : p-nitrophenol is more acidic than m-nitrophenol and o-nitrophenol. Statement (II) : Ethanol will give immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: pKa: p-nitrophenol 7.15 < o 7.23 (intramolecular H-bond) < m 8.4. I true.
Lucas: only 3° alcohols turn turbid at once; ethanol (1°) shows no turbidity at room temperature. II false.
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Phenolic group can be identified by a positive:
sol: Phenol + phthalic anhydride (conc. H_{2}SO_{4}) → phenolphthalein (pink in alkali).

pyq.q: Phenol treated with chloroform in presence of sodium hydroxide, which further hydrolysed in presence of an acid results
sol: Reimer–Tiemann: phenoxide + :CCl_{2} → after hydrolysis, 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde).

pyq.q: Which one of the following, with HBr will give a phenol?
sol: HBr cleaves an alkyl aryl ether at the alkyl–O bond: Ar–O–CH_{3} → ArOH + CH_{3}Br (the Ar–O bond is too strong).
Only anisole has O directly on the ring.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: Alcohols react both as nucleophiles and electrophiles. Reason R: Alcohols react with active metals such as sodium, potassium and aluminum to yield corresponding alkoxides and liberate hydrogen. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: A: O lone pair attacks (nucleophile); protonated –OH_{2}^{+} lets C be attacked (electrophile). True.
R: true (acidic O–H), but it describes acidity, not the dual nucleophile/electrophile role.
o: A is false but R is true.
A is true but R is false.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: pK_{a} value of phenol is 10.0 while that of ethanol is 15.9. Reason R: Ethanol is stronger acid than phenol. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: A: correct values. R: lower pKa means stronger acid — phenol (resonance-stabilised phenoxide) is the stronger acid. R false.
o: A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

pyq.q: The reactions which produce alcohol as the product are : A. CH_{4} + O_{2} (Mo_{2}O_{3}, Δ) B. 2CH_{3}CH_{3} + 3O_{2} ((CH_{3}COO)_{2}Mn, Δ) C. (CH_{3})_{3}CH + KMnO_{4} D. 2CH_{4} + O_{2} (Cu/523 K/100 atm) E. CH_{3}–CH=CH–CH_{3} + KMnO_{4}/H^{+}
sol: A → HCHO; B → CH_{3}COOH; E → 2 CH_{3}COOH (oxidative cleavage).
C: the 3° C–H is oxidised → (CH_{3})_{3}COH. D: controlled oxidation → CH_{3}OH.

pyq.q: R_{f} value for 2-methylpropene in a solvent system (Ethyl acetate + ether) is 0.42. 2-methylpropene is treated with dilute H_{2}SO_{4} to give major organic product (X). R_{f} value for (X) in the same solvent system under identical condition will be:
sol: Acid-catalysed hydration (Markovnikov) → X = tert-butyl alcohol.
The polar –OH binds the silica more strongly → it travels less: R_{f} below 0.42 → 0.12.

pyq.q: 4.7 g of phenol is heated with Zn to give product X. If this reaction goes to 60% completion then the number of moles of compound X formed will be ____ × 10^{−2}. (Nearest Integer) (Given molar mass in g mol^{−1} : H : 1, C : 12, O : 16 )
sol: Phenol + Zn → benzene (X) + ZnO, 1 : 1.

pyq.q: Consider the reaction: C_{6}H_{5}–O–CH_{2}–C_{6}H_{5} + HI → Product. Statement I: In the above reaction, product formed will be a mixture of benzyl alcohol and iodobenzene. Statement II : In the above reaction, the –O–CH_{2}– bond is cleaved to give the product. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: The Ph–O bond (partial double bond) is not broken; I^{−} attacks the benzylic CH_{2} → phenol + benzyl iodide.
So I (benzyl alcohol + iodobenzene) is false; II is true.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Benzene is treated with oleum to produce compound (X) which when further heated with molten sodium hydroxide followed by acidification produces compound (Y). The compound Y is treated with zinc metal to produce compound (Z). Identify the structure of compound (Z) from the following option.
sol: X = benzenesulphonic acid → fused NaOH, then acid → Y = phenol.
Zn dust reduces phenol → Z = benzene.

pyq.q: Common name of Benzene-1, 2-diol is
sol: Benzene-1,2-diol: catechol; 1,3: resorcinol; 1,4: quinol (hydroquinone). o-Cresol is 2-methylphenol.

pyq.q: A toxic compound "A" when reacted with NaCN in aqueous acidic medium yields an edible cooking component and food preservative "B". "B" is converted to "C" by diborane and can be used as an additive to petrol to reduce emission. "C" upon reaction with oleum at 140°C yields an inhalable anesthetic "D". Identify "A", "B", "C" & "D", respectively :
sol: B (vinegar, preservative) = acetic acid; B_{2}H_{6} reduces it to C = ethanol (petrol additive).
Ethanol + H_{2}SO_{4} at 413 K → D = diethyl ether (anaesthetic). The toxic A that gives acetic acid with CN^{−} (C–C formation) is methanol.
o: Acetaldehyde; 2-hydroxypropanoic acid; propanoic acid; dipropyl ether
Methanol; acetic acid; ethanol; diethyl ether

pyq.q: Number of molecules from below which cannot give iodoform reaction is: Ethanol, Isopropyl alcohol, Bromoacetone, 2-Butanol, 2-Butanone, Butanal, 2-Pentanone, 3-Pentanone, Pentanal and 3-Pentanol.
sol: Iodoform needs CH_{3}CO– or CH_{3}CH(OH)– (ethanol is the only 1° alcohol that works).
Cannot: butanal, 3-pentanone, pentanal, 3-pentanol → 4. (Bromoacetone still has the CH_{3}CO–.)

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Acidity of α-hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones is responsible for Aldol reaction. Statement II : Reaction between benzaldehyde and ethanal will NOT give Cross - Aldol product. In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
sol: I: base removes an acidic α-H to form the enolate. True.
II: ethanal's enolate adds to benzaldehyde (Claisen–Schmidt) → cinnamaldehyde, a cross-aldol product. False.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

pyq.q: In the Claisen-Schmidt reaction to prepare 351 g of dibenzalacetone using 87 g of acetone, the amount of benzaldehyde required is ____ g. (Nearest integer)
sol: 351/234 = 1.5 mol product (acetone 87/58 = 1.5 mol fits) → 3 mol benzaldehyde × 106 = 318 g.

pyq.q: Which among the following aldehydes is most reactive towards nucleophilic addition reactions?
sol: Nucleophilic addition is fastest when the carbonyl C is least crowded and least electron-rich.
HCHO (two H) > CH_{3}CHO > C_{2}H_{5}CHO > C_{3}H_{7}CHO.

pyq.q: "P" is an optically active compound with molecular formula C_{6}H_{12}O. When 'P' is treated with 2, 4-dinitrophenylhydrazine, it gives a positive test. However, in presence of Tollens reagent, "P" gives a negative test. Predict the structure of "P".
sol: 2,4-DNP + and Tollens − → a ketone.
Optically active → a chiral carbon: only 3-methylpentan-2-one (C-3 has H, CH_{3}, C_{2}H_{5}, COCH_{3}).

pyq.q: Match List-I (Test) with List-II (Identification): (A) Bayer's test (B) Ceric ammonium nitrate test (C) Phthalein dye test (D) Schiff's test; (I) Phenol (II) Aldehyde (III) Alcoholic-OH group (IV) Unsaturation
sol: Baeyer (cold KMnO_{4}) — C=C; ceric ammonium nitrate — red with alcohols; phthalein dye — phenols; Schiff's reagent — aldehydes (pink).

pyq.q: Two moles of benzaldehyde and one mole of acetone under alkaline conditions using aqueous NaOH after heating gives x as the major product. The number of π bonds in the product x is
sol: x = dibenzalacetone, C_{6}H_{5}CH=CH–CO–CH=CH–C_{6}H_{5}.
π bonds: 2 rings × 3 + 2 C=C + 1 C=O = 9.

pyq.q: Which of the following compounds will give silver mirror with ammoniacal silver nitrate? (A) Formic acid (B) Formaldehyde (C) Benzaldehyde (D) Acetone
sol: Tollens is reduced by all aldehydes (aliphatic and aromatic) and by HCOOH (it has an H–C=O).
Ketones (acetone) do not react.

pyq.q: Match List - I (Mixture of Compounds) with List - II (Reagent used to distinguish): A. Diethyl amine + Ethyl amine B. Acetaldehyde + Acetone C. Ethanol + Phenol D. Benzoic acid + Cinnamic acid; I. Bromine water II. CHCl_{3} + KOH, Δ III. Neutral FeCl_{3} IV. Ammonical silver nitrate
sol: 1° amine: carbylamine (foul isocyanide). Aldehyde: Tollens. Phenol: violet with neutral FeCl_{3}.
Cinnamic acid (C=C) decolourises bromine water; benzoic acid does not.

pyq.q: An organic compound "P" of molecular formula C_{6}H_{12}O_{3} gives positive Iodoform test but negative Tollen's test. When "P" is treated with dilute acid, it produces "Q". "Q" gives positive Tollen's test and also iodoform test. The structure of "P" is :
sol: Iodoform + and Tollens − → P has CH_{3}CO– and no free CHO.
Dilute acid hydrolyses a dimethyl ACETAL to an aldehyde: P = CH_{3}COCH_{2}CH(OCH_{3})_{2} → Q = CH_{3}COCH_{2}CHO (Tollens + and iodoform +). (Option 4 is a ketal → no aldehyde.)

pyq.q: A molecule (X) CH_{3}–CH=CH–O–C(CH_{3})=CH_{2} under mild acidic condition is hydrolysed to produce (Y) and (Z). Identify the correct statements about (Y) and (Z). A. Both (Y) and (Z) have same molar mass. B. (Y) and (Z) can be distinguished from each other by NaHCO_{3}. C. (Y) and (Z) react with HCN with same rates. D. (Y) and (Z) undergo addition reaction with 2,4-DNP.
sol: Each enol-ether half becomes a carbonyl: Y = propanal, Z = acetone (both C_{3}H_{6}O, 58 — A ✓).
Neither is acidic (B ✗); the aldehyde adds HCN faster (C ✗); both form 2,4-DNP derivatives (D ✓).

pyq.q: Match List - I (Reagents) with List - II (Reaction Name, involving aldehydes): A. H_{2}, Pd–BaSO_{4} B. SnCl_{2}, HCl C. CrO_{2}Cl_{2}, CS_{2} D. CO, HCl, Anhyd. AlCl_{3}; I. Etard Reaction II. Rosenmund Reduction III. Gatterman - Koch Reaction IV. Stephen Reaction
sol: Rosenmund: RCOCl + H_{2}/Pd–BaSO_{4}. Stephen: RCN + SnCl_{2}/HCl. Etard: toluene + CrO_{2}Cl_{2}. Gattermann–Koch: benzene + CO/HCl.

pyq.q: The compounds which give positive Fehling's test are : (A) benzaldehyde (B) acetophenone (C) HOCH_{2}–CO–(CHOH)_{3}–CH_{2}OH (D) CH_{3}CHO (E) phenylacetaldehyde (C_{6}H_{5}CH_{2}CHO)
sol: Fehling is reduced by aliphatic aldehydes (incl. PhCH_{2}CHO, where CHO is on an sp^{3} C) and α-hydroxy ketones like fructose.
Aromatic aldehydes (CHO on the ring) and simple ketones do not.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Consider the hydration R–CO–R + H_{2}O ⇌ R_{2}C(OH)_{2} with equilibrium constant K. Statement (I) : In the case of formaldehyde (H–CO–H), K is about 2280, due to small substituents, hydration is faster. Statement (II) : In the case of trichloro acetaldehyde (Cl_{3}C–CHO), K is about 2000 due to -I effect of -Cl. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: Small groups (HCHO) and strongly electron-withdrawing groups (CCl_{3} in chloral) both favour the gem-diol. Both true (chloral hydrate is a stable solid).
o: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

pyq.q: Aman has been asked to synthesise the molecule 1-acetylcyclopentene (x). He thought of preparing the molecule using an aldol condensation reaction. He found a few cyclic alkenes in his laboratory. He thought of performing ozonolysis reaction on alkene to produce a dicarbonyl compound followed by aldol reaction to prepare "x". Predict the suitable alkene that can lead to the formation of "x".
sol: 1-Methylcyclohexene → ozonolysis → 6-oxoheptanal (CH_{3}CO(CH_{2})_{4}CHO).
Intramolecular aldol: the CH_{2} α to the ketone attacks the CHO → five-membered ring; dehydration → 1-acetylcyclopentene.

pyq.q: Which of the following arrangements with respect to their reactivity in nucleophilic addition reaction is correct?
sol: Ketone (two groups, more crowded/electron-rich) is least reactive.
Among aldehydes: p-CH_{3} (+I) lowers, p-NO_{2} (−R) raises the C=O carbon's positive charge.

pyq.q: Match List - I with List - II: (A) RCN → (i) SnCl_{2}, HCl (ii) H_{3}O^{+} → RCHO (B) C_{6}H_{5}COCl → H_{2}, Pd-BaSO_{4} → C_{6}H_{5}CHO (C) C_{6}H_{5}CH_{3} → (i) CrO_{2}Cl_{2}, CS_{2} (ii) H_{3}O^{+} → C_{6}H_{5}CHO (D) C_{6}H_{6} → (i) CO, HCl (ii) anhydrous AlCl_{3}/CuCl → C_{6}H_{5}CHO; (I) Etard reaction (II) Gatterman-Koch reaction (III) Rosenmund reduction (IV) Stephen reaction
sol: Nitrile + SnCl_{2}/HCl → Stephen. Acid chloride + H_{2}/Pd–BaSO_{4} → Rosenmund. Toluene + chromyl chloride → Etard. Benzene + CO/HCl → Gattermann–Koch.

pyq.q: Both acetaldehyde and acetone (individually) undergo which of the following reactions? A. Iodoform Reaction B. Cannizaro Reaction C. Aldol Condensation D. Tollen's Test E. Clemmensen Reduction
sol: Both have CH_{3}CO– (iodoform ✓) and α-H (aldol ✓); both C=O are reduced by Zn-Hg/HCl (Clemmensen ✓).
Cannizzaro needs no α-H (✗); Tollens needs an aldehyde (acetone ✗).

pyq.q: From the compounds given below, number of compounds which give positive Fehling's test is: Benzaldehyde, Acetaldehyde, Acetone, Acetophenone, Methanal, 4-nitrobenzaldehyde, cyclohexane carbaldehyde.
sol: Fehling + : aliphatic aldehydes — acetaldehyde, methanal, cyclohexanecarbaldehyde → 3.
Aromatic aldehydes and ketones are negative.

pyq.q: In the Claisen-Schmidt reaction to prepare, dibenzalacetone from 5.3 g of benzaldehyde, a total of 3.51 g of product was obtained. The percentage yield in this reaction was ______%.
sol: 5.3 g PhCHO = 0.05 mol → theoretical 0.025 mol dibenzalacetone × 234 = 5.85 g.

pyq.q: C_{6}H_{5}COCl → H_{2}, Pd-BaSO_{4} → C_{6}H_{5}CHO. This reduction reaction is known as:
sol: Acid chloride + H_{2} over poisoned Pd (BaSO_{4}) stops at the aldehyde: Rosenmund reduction.

pyq.q: The compound formed by the reaction of ethanal with semicarbazide contains _____ number of nitrogen atoms.
sol: CH_{3}CHO + H_{2}N–NH–CO–NH_{2} → CH_{3}CH=N–NH–CO–NH_{2} + H_{2}O.
All 3 N of semicarbazide stay → 3.

pyq.q: Salicylaldehyde is synthesized from phenol, when reacted with
sol: Reimer–Tiemann: CHCl_{3} + NaOH → salicylaldehyde. (CCl_{4} + NaOH would give salicylic acid; CO_{2} is Kolbe.)

pyq.q: m-chlorobenzaldehyde on treatment with 50% KOH solution yields
sol: No α-H + conc. alkali → Cannizzaro: one molecule is oxidised (carboxylate), one reduced (alcohol).
The aryl C–Cl is untouched by KOH.

pyq.q: Identify the name reaction: C_{6}H_{6} → CO, HCl, Anhyd. AlCl_{3}/CuCl → C_{6}H_{5}CHO
sol: Formylation of benzene with CO + HCl (AlCl_{3}/CuCl) is the Gattermann–Koch reaction.

pyq.q: Match the LIST-I (Compound) with LIST-II (Test): A. cyclohexanol B. cyclohexylamine C. cyclohexanecarbaldehyde D. phenol; I. Hinsberg's reagent test II. Phthalein dye test III. Lucas test IV. Tollen's test
sol: Alcohol — Lucas; amine — Hinsberg (C_{6}H_{5}SO_{2}Cl); aldehyde — Tollens; phenol — phthalein dye.

pyq.q: The compound A, C_{8}H_{8}O_{2} reacts with acetophenone to form a single product via cross-Aldol condensation. The compound A on reaction with conc. NaOH forms a substituted benzyl alcohol as one of the two products. The compound A is :
sol: A must be an aldehyde with no α-H (single cross-aldol product; Cannizzaro with conc. NaOH) and formula C_{8}H_{8}O_{2}.
4-Methoxybenzaldehyde (CH_{3}O–C_{6}H_{4}–CHO, M = 136) fits; 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde is C_{7}H_{6}O_{2}.

pyq.q: Match List - I (Functional group, detection) with List - II (Change observed during detection): A. Unsaturation (Baeyer's test) B. Alcoholic group (Ceric ammonium nitrate test) C. Aldehyde group (Tollen's reagent) D. Phenolic group (FeCl_{3} test); I. Red colour appears II. Silver mirror appears III. Violet colour appears IV. Discharge of pink colour
sol: Baeyer: KMnO_{4} pink is discharged. CAN: red with alcohols. Tollens: silver mirror. Neutral FeCl_{3}: violet with phenols.

pyq.q: Iodoform test can differentiate between A. Methanol and Ethanol B. CH_{3}COOH and CH_{3}CH_{2}COOH C. Cyclohexene and cyclohexanone D. Diethyl ether and Pentan-3-one E. Anisole and acetone
sol: A pair is told apart only if exactly one member gives CHI_{3}.
A: ethanol +, methanol −. E: acetone +, anisole −. In B, C, D neither member reacts (acids, cyclohexanone and pentan-3-one have no CH_{3}CO–).

pyq.q: Which of the following statements are TRUE about Haloform reaction?: A. Sodium hypochlorite reacts with KI to give KOI. B. KOI is a reducing agent. C. α,β-unsaturated methylketone (CH_{3}–CH=CH–CO–CH_{3}) will give iodoform reaction. D. Isopropyl alcohol will not give iodoform test. E. Methanoic acid will give positive iodoform test.
sol: A ✓ (NaOCl + KI → KOI + NaCl). B ✗: hypoiodite is an oxidising agent. C ✓: it still has CH_{3}CO–.
D ✗: isopropyl alcohol is oxidised to acetone → positive. E ✗: HCOOH has no CH_{3}.

pyq.q: A student is given one compound among the following compounds that gives positive test with Tollen's reagent: A 2-methoxyoxolane (cyclic acetal) B 3-methoxyoxolane C oxolan-2-ol (cyclic hemiacetal) D oxolan-3-ol. The compound is :
sol: A cyclic hemiacetal (–O–CH(OH)–) opens in solution to an open-chain aldehyde (4-hydroxybutanal) → Tollens +.
Acetals (A) are stable in base; B and D are just ether-alcohols.

pyq.q: 'x' is the product which is obtained from the hydrolysis of prop-1-yne in the presence of mercuric sulphate under dilute acidic medium at 333 K. 'y' is the product which is obtained by the reaction of ethane nitrile with methyl magnesium bromide in dry ether followed by hydrolysis. IUPAC name of product obtained from 'x' and 'y' in the presence of barium hydroxide followed by heating is :
sol: x = acetone (Markovnikov hydration of propyne); y = acetone (CH_{3}CN + CH_{3}MgBr → imine → ketone).
Aldol of acetone (Ba(OH)_{2}) then dehydration → mesityl oxide (CH_{3})_{2}C=CH–CO–CH_{3}: 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one.

pyq.q: The unsaturated ether CH_{3}–CH=CH–O–CH=CH_{2} on acidic hydrolysis gives CH_{3}CH_{2}CHO and CH_{3}CHO. Based on this, predict the solution/reagent that will help to distinguish "P" and "Q" obtained in: CH_{3}–CH=CH–O–C(CH_{3})=CH_{2} → H_{3}O^{+}, Δ → P + Q
sol: P = propanal, Q = acetone. Both form 2,4-DNP derivatives and bisulphite adducts; neither is an alcohol.
Only the aliphatic aldehyde reduces Fehling solution (red Cu_{2}O).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Cross aldol condensation between two different aldehydes will always produce four different products. Statement II: When semicarbazide reacts with a mixture of benzaldehyde and acetophenone under optimum pH, it forms a condensation product with acetophenone only. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: I: if one aldehyde has no α-H (e.g. HCHO, PhCHO), fewer products form — "always four" is false.
II: the aldehyde (more reactive C=O) condenses readily; it is not "acetophenone only". False.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

pyq.q: 'x' is the product which is obtained from propanenitrile and stannous chloride in the presence of hydrochloric acid followed by hydrolysis. 'y' is the product which is obtained from the but-2-ene by the ozonolysis followed by hydrolysis. From the following, which product is not obtained when one mole of 'x' and one mole of 'y' react with each other in the presence of alkali followed by heating ?
sol: x = propanal (Stephen), y = ethanal. Possible aldol condensations: y+y → but-2-enal; x+x → 2-methylpent-2-enal; enolate of x + y → 2-methylbut-2-enal; enolate of y + x → pent-2-enal.
3-Methylbut-2-enal (CH_{3})_{2}C=CHCHO would need acetone — not formed.

pyq.q: 'x' is the product which is obtained from benzene by reacting it with carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride in the presence of cuprous chloride. 'y' is the major product obtained from the benzene by reacting it with ethanoyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous AlCl_{3}. Product (major) obtained by heating x and y in the presence of alkali is z. Total number of π (pi) electrons in z is _____
sol: x = benzaldehyde (Gattermann–Koch), y = acetophenone. Claisen–Schmidt → z = chalcone C_{6}H_{5}CH=CH–CO–C_{6}H_{5}.
π electrons: two rings 6 + 6, C=C 2, C=O 2 → 16.

pyq.q: An organic compound (X) with molecular formula C_{3}H_{6}O is not readily oxidised. On reduction it gives C_{3}H_{8}O(Y) which reacts with HBr to give a bromide (Z) which is converted to Grignard reagent. This Grignard reagent on reaction with (X) followed by hydrolysis give 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol. Compounds (X), (Y) and (Z) respectively are:
sol: Not readily oxidised → ketone: X = acetone → Y propan-2-ol → Z 2-bromopropane → (CH_{3})_{2}CHMgBr.

pyq.q: Consider the following reactions. From these reactions which reaction will give carboxylic acid as a major product? (A) R–C≡N → (i) H^{+}/H_{2}O, mild condition (B) R–MgX → (i) CO_{2} (ii) H_{3}O^{+} (C) R–C≡N → (i) SnCl_{2}/HCl (ii) H_{3}O^{+} (D) R·CH_{2}·OH → PCC (E) C_{6}H_{5}COCl → (i) H_{2}/Pd–BaSO_{4} (ii) Br_{2} water
sol: A: mild hydrolysis stops at the amide. C: Stephen → aldehyde. D: PCC stops at the aldehyde.
B: RMgX + CO_{2} → RCOOH. E: Rosenmund → PhCHO, then Br_{2} water oxidises it → PhCOOH.

pyq.q: CH_{3}CH_{2}–OH → (i) Jone's Reagent (ii) KMnO_{4} (iii) NaOH, CaO, Δ → P. Consider the above reaction sequence and identify the major product P.
sol: Ethanol → CH_{3}COOH (oxidation); soda-lime decarboxylation of the sodium salt removes CO_{2} → CH_{4}.

pyq.q: The molecular formula of second homologue in the homologous series of mono carboxylic acids is
sol: Series C_{n}H_{2n}O_{2}: HCOOH (n = 1) is the first, CH_{3}COOH (C_{2}H_{4}O_{2}) the second.

pyq.q: RMgI when treated with ice cold water liberated a gas which occupied 1.4 dm^{3}/g at STP. The gas produced is further reacted with iodine in presence of HIO_{3} to give compound (X). Compound (X) in presence of Na and dry ether produced compound (Y). Molar mass of compound (Y) is ____ g mol^{−1}. (Nearest integer)
sol: M = 22.4 L/mol ÷ 1.4 L/g = 16 → CH_{4} (RMgI = CH_{3}MgI).
CH_{4} + I_{2} (HIO_{3} removes HI) → CH_{3}I → Wurtz → C_{2}H_{6}: M = 30.

pyq.q: Grignard reagent RMgBr (P) reacts with water and forms a gas (Q). One gram of Q occupies 1.4 dm^{3} at STP. (P) on reaction with dry ice in dry ether followed by H_{3}O^{+} forms a compound (Z). 0.1 mole of (Z) will weigh ____ g. (Nearest integer)
sol: Q has M = 22.4/1.4 = 16 → CH_{4}, so P = CH_{3}MgBr.
CH_{3}MgBr + CO_{2} → CH_{3}COOH (60): 0.1 mol = 6 g.

pyq.q: The correct order of acidic strength of the major products formed in the given reactions, is : A. PhNH_{2} → (1) NaNO_{2} + HCl (< 5°C) (2) CuCN (3) H_{3}O^{+}/Δ → [A] B. CH_{3}CH_{2}CHO → [Ag(NH_{3})_{2}]^{+}, OH^{−}, Δ → [B] C. CH_{4} + O_{2} → (i) Mo_{2}O_{3} (ii) Na_{2}Cr_{2}O_{7}/H^{+} → [C] D. PhCH_{2}MgBr + CO_{2} → dry ether, H_{3}O^{+} → [D]
sol: A benzoic acid (pKa 4.20); B propanoic acid (4.87); C methanoic acid (3.75); D phenylacetic acid (4.31).
Lower pKa = stronger: C > A > D > B.
